waive.P1_NoOpTwice: This file records equivalent mutants only (changes no property can notice for engines that follow the design); property coverage is shown by mutations.json.

mutations.name: drop-client-seq-duplicate-check-honest-clients
mutations.why: store.append without the (client, seq) check, against engines that follow section 5, with old sockets left open so late copies of a submit do reach store.append after the resend.
mutations.equivalent: Every copy of one seq that an honest engine can still have on the wire carries the same base: a copy with another base is sent only after a foreign change took the old base + 1 (invariant 5, checked as P5). So when a late copy arrives after its twin was appended, head > base and the base check answers stale where the duplicate check would have answered ack; the engine has already confirmed that seq from the change frame that preceded the answer on its socket, and ignores both answers.

mutations.name: any-own-change-is-ack
mutations.why: The lost-ack rule treats every change from this client at confirmed + 1 as the ack of the in-flight, without comparing seq and without requiring a live in-flight.
mutations.equivalent: An own change at confirmed + 1 always carries the in-flight's seq: the engine sends seq n + 1 only after seq n is confirmed, a seq is appended at most once (invariant 2) and only at base + 1 (invariant 1), and the copies that carry the seq after a doom or stale are dead. FramesCovered checks exactly this in every config, so the seq comparison never decides anything.

mutations.name: any-own-change-is-ack-fenced-sockets
mutations.why: The same change with the design's socket handling (superseded sockets ignored) and the F1 fence.
mutations.equivalent: As for any-own-change-is-ack: with superseded sockets ignored an own change reaches a socket other than the submitter's only through catch-up, at the in-flight's base + 1 and with its seq.
